metaDescription: Five cordless jigsaws under $100 compared on stroke length, orbital settings, brushless motors, blade change and whether the battery is in the box.
expertTake: A good cordless jigsaw under $100 is a matter of picking the right bundle, because the motor matters less than the blade and the battery. The Makita XVJ04Z is the best overall: a brushless 3,000 SPM motor, three orbital settings and a soft-start mode on a major 18V platform, sold as a bare tool. The WOODERS brushless kit is the best complete package, the Greenworks is the pick for 24V owners and the SEESII is the cheapest way to get nine blades and two batteries. Skip this tier for thick hardwood and long straight rips.
introParagraphs: A jigsaw cuts by moving a thin blade up and down, and that simple motion does a lot of work for a small tool: curves in plywood, cutouts in countertops, notches in trim. The blade is a consumable and the cut quality owes more to it than to the motor.

At a low price the choices come down to platform, battery and blade handling, not horsepower. This guide explains what to look for in a budget cordless jigsaw, which compromises are fine for home projects and which will frustrate you. The quick picks are above, and the reviews below match each saw to a job.

products.name: Makita XVJ04Z 18V LXT Brushless Cordless Jig Saw, Tool Only
products.description:
The XVJ04Z is the best jigsaw here because it adds a feature that budget saws skip: a soft no-load mode that ramps the blade speed up slowly until it engages the work. That slow start keeps the blade from skipping across the surface at the start of a cut, which is the most common way to ruin a visible edge. A brushless motor delivers variable speed up to 3,000 strokes per minute, which is the same top rate as the Greenworks and a little below the WOODERS at 3,200.

Three orbital settings plus a straight-cut mode matter more than they sound. Orbital action pushes the blade forward on the upstroke so it bites aggressively in wood and clears chips, while straight cutting keeps it rigid for metal and clean laminate. A saw with no orbital choice has to compromise. Against the B+D, which offers tool-free blade changes but no orbital control on its listing, the Makita gives you the ability to match action to material.

It is sold bare, so the true cost depends on owning an 18V LXT battery. If you do, it is the best buy by a wide margin. Check that the blade is fully seated and the shoe is square before each cut, and use tape on the cut line for veneered plywood to reduce splintering.
products.bestFor: Makita LXT owners and buyers building a long-term battery platform.
pros: Soft no-load start prevents blade skipping at the cut start
Brushless motor reaches 3,000 strokes per minute
Three orbital settings plus a straight mode
LXT battery fits a very wide tool range
cons: Bare tool, so battery and charger cost extra
Higher up-front outlay than the no-name kits
No blades included in the box

products.name: WOODERS 20V Brushless Cordless Jig Saw, 4.0Ah Battery, 3,200 SPM
products.description:
The WOODERS is the best complete package because it ships with a brushless motor, a 4.0 Ah battery and a counterweight system. It reaches 3,200 strokes per minute, the highest rate in the roundup, and has a full 1-inch stroke. Stroke length is the distance the blade travels up and down, and a longer stroke clears more chips per pass and cuts faster in thick stock.

An internal counterweight moves opposite the blade to cancel some vibration. That is a real benefit, since jigsaw vibration is the main reason cuts wander and hands tire, and it is a feature that normally appears on more expensive saws. The 4.0 Ah battery is the largest in a budget jigsaw kit here, so it will run through a full afternoon of curves.

The weak point is the brand: a small seller with no deep platform means spare batteries may be hard to find. Compared with the SEESII, which gives two 2.0 Ah packs and nine blades, the WOODERS has one larger battery and a stronger motor design. Replace the stock blade with a quality one for the material, and keep the saw's base flat on the work.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a brushless saw, a big battery and low vibration in a single box.
pros: Highest stroke rate here at 3,200 SPM
Full 1-inch stroke clears chips quickly
Counterweight system reduces vibration
4.0 Ah battery lasts a long session
cons: No-name platform makes spare batteries uncertain
Single battery means a wait when it drains
Blade selection in the box is limited

products.name: Greenworks 24V Brushless 1-Inch Cordless Jig Saw, 4.0Ah Battery
products.description:
The Greenworks sells a brushless 1-inch-stroke jigsaw with a 4.0 Ah battery on its own 24V platform. The 24V pack, listed as a USB-capable battery, can also charge a phone, a useful trick on a job site. Greenworks claims the pack delivers fade-free power, meaning voltage holds steady until the cell is nearly empty, which keeps the blade speed constant late in a long cut.

Four orbital settings let you match the blade action to the work, and a tool-free blade clamp swaps blades in seconds. Against the WOODERS, it matches the stroke length and gives up 200 strokes per minute, but it belongs to a platform with mowers, trimmers and blowers that use the same battery. If you already own Greenworks tools, that is the argument.

If you do not, the price is competitive but the platform is less common among woodworkers. Greenworks tools are better known for yard equipment, so expect fewer shop tools to add later. Use sharp blades and let the saw's weight do the work, and check the clamp for wear after several hundred blade changes.
products.bestFor: Greenworks owners and anyone who wants a brushless saw that shares a battery with yard tools.
pros: Brushless motor with a full 1-inch stroke
Four orbital settings for different materials
USB-capable 4.0 Ah battery is included
Battery fits Greenworks yard tools
cons: Platform is stronger in yard tools than shop tools
24V battery will not fit 18V or 20V tools

products.name: SEESII Cordless Jigsaw, Two 2.0Ah Batteries, 9 Blades, 45-Degree Bevel

specList.label: Blades included
specList.value: Nine, for wood, metal and PVC

products.description:
The SEESII is the best value if you want to start cutting without buying anything else. It includes two 2.0 Ah batteries and nine blades covering wood, metal and PVC, so you can swap batteries instead of waiting and swap blades instead of shopping. In a jigsaw, where blade choice makes more difference than motor choice, that bundle is worth a lot.

It bevels 45 degrees to each side and has four orbital settings. A thumb-push quick-release lets you change blades by pushing and pulling, a design that is fast but depends on a spring that can wear. Against the WOODERS, you get two smaller batteries instead of one larger one and nine blades instead of one, but no brushless motor listed.

That last point matters for ownership. A brushed motor wears out its brushes over years of use, so the SEESII is a good tool for a few big projects and a worse one for a busy shop. Expect it to run warm in long cuts, and rest it between curves. Use the right blade for the material, such as fine-tooth for metal and coarse for wood.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers who want batteries and blades included for mixed materials.
pros: Two batteries mean one is always charged
Nine blades included for several materials
Bevels 45 degrees to either side
Thumb-push blade release is quick
cons: Motor is not listed as brushless
2.0 Ah batteries are small for long sessions

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX POWERCONNECT BDCJS20B Jig Saw, Tool Only
products.description:
The BDCJS20B is the home-oriented choice. Its tool-free blade change accepts both U-shank and T-shank blades, which gives you the widest range of blades on the market, and the listing highlights straight, curved, angled and plunge cuts. A plunge cut lets you start in the middle of a panel, which is how you make sink cutouts.

It is sold bare, so you need a 20V MAX POWERCONNECT battery. The pack is cheap to buy and shared with a large range of home tools, from trimmers to vacuums, which makes it the easy platform to grow. Against the Makita it is a simpler tool with no listed soft start or orbital control, so it is best for light projects: plywood shelves, craft cutouts and trim.

The limitation is stamina. Heavy use in thick lumber will tire the motor and drain the pack, and the build is aimed at occasional work. For a household that wants a jigsaw in the closet for a project a few times a year, it is a sensible, inexpensive choice. Keep spare blades, because the stock blade is general-purpose.
products.bestFor: Existing B+D 20V MAX owners who want a simple jigsaw for occasional projects.
pros: Accepts both U and T shank blades tool-free
Handles straight, curved, angled and plunge cuts
POWERCONNECT battery fits many home tools
Simple and easy for beginners
cons: Bare tool, so battery and charger cost extra
No listed orbital control or brushless motor

buyingCriteria.explanation: Stroke length is how far the blade travels up and down, and stroke rate is how often. The WOODERS and Greenworks have 1-inch strokes, with the WOODERS at 3,200 SPM and the Greenworks and Makita at 3,000. A longer stroke clears chips from thick stock, while a high rate smooths cuts in thin stock. Look for at least 3/4 inch of stroke for 2x material. A practical rule is to match stroke to thickness: 3/4 inch of stroke is fine for 3/4 inch plywood, but a 2x4 wants the full 1 inch, which only the WOODERS and Greenworks list.

Orbital action swings the blade forward as it rises, so it bites aggressively and clears chips. The Makita offers three settings plus straight, the SEESII and Greenworks four settings and the B+D does not list any. Use high orbital for fast rough cuts in softwood, and straight for metal and clean veneer. A saw without it can only cut at one aggressiveness. On a ladder or overhead cutout, orbital action set too high makes the saw hop, so turn it down and let the blade cut at its own pace.

A jigsaw's finish is mostly a blade question: more teeth per inch cut smoother but slower, fewer teeth cut faster and rougher. The SEESII's nine blades cover more materials than any other kit here. A good T-shank blade costs only a few dollars and transforms a cheap saw, so budget for a few. If you cut laminate countertops, use a fine-tooth reverse-tooth blade and keep orbital at zero, whichever saw you own.

Brushless motors in the Makita, WOODERS and Greenworks run cooler and last longer per charge, while the SEESII and B+D lists do not claim brushless. If you cut for hours at a time, brushless pays back; for a few projects a year, it does not. Even a good brushless motor will not rescue a cheap blade, so treat the blades in each kit as a starter set.

Kits with batteries, like the WOODERS, Greenworks and SEESII, are ready out of the box, while the Makita and B+D are bare. Check which platform you already own, since a bare tool is a bargain only with a matching pack. The Greenworks 24V pack fits no 18V or 20V tool. A pack that charges in about an hour is more useful than one with bigger capacity that takes three, so check the charger rating as well.

A counterweight like the WOODERS's cuts vibration, and a soft start like the Makita's prevents skipping at the start of a cut. Both features improve accuracy on visible edges. Without them you must hold the saw down firmly and start slowly. Hold the saw against the work before you pull the trigger, because the shoe, not the blade, sets the angle of the cut.

specDecoder.meaning: SPM counts how many times the blade moves up and down each minute. Faster rates cut faster and smoother in thin stock. Because a blade moves both up and down, only the upstroke cuts in a typical jigsaw, which is why orbital action pushes the blade forward as it rises.
specDecoder.watchFor: A higher rate does not help in thick or dense wood. The WOODERS's 3,200 and Makita's 3,000 are close in practice.

specDecoder.meaning: Stroke length is the distance the blade travels per stroke. A longer stroke clears more chips and cuts faster in thick stock. If a listing quotes only the maximum stroke rate, remember that the trigger is variable and you will rarely run it flat out.
specDecoder.watchFor: Listings sometimes skip this. Both the WOODERS and Greenworks give 1 inch.

specDecoder.meaning: Orbital action tilts the blade forward on the upstroke for aggressive cutting. Settings are numbered from zero to three or four. Settings numbered from zero use a straight vertical stroke, which is the cleanest for veneers and metal.
specDecoder.watchFor: Use zero for metal and thin laminate to avoid chatter and chipping.

specDecoder.meaning: T-shank blades lock in with a tab, and U-shank blades use a hook. T-shank is the modern standard and widely available. A tool-free clamp also saves time on jobs with many blade changes, such as cutouts in different materials.
specDecoder.watchFor: The B+D accepts both, but many saws accept only T-shank.

specDecoder.meaning: A brushless motor uses electronic commutation and has no brushes to wear. It runs cooler and longer per charge. If a listing does not say brushless, assume a standard brushed motor and judge the saw accordingly.
specDecoder.watchFor: Verify on the listing. The SEESII and B+D do not state it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stroke and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stroke length and strokes per minute, giving the WOODERS credit for 3,200 SPM and a 1-inch stroke. We checked whether orbital settings, bevel range and soft start were listed rather than assuming them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Orbital and bevel control
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted orbital settings and bevel range, since they let a saw adapt to materials. The Makita, Greenworks and SEESII scored best. Batteries were compared by capacity and count, so the SEESII's pair of 2.0 Ah packs was weighed against single 4.0 Ah packs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blades and batteries in the box
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted blades and batteries included, since they decide whether you can start cutting immediately. We treated blade quality as an ownership item and credited kits that include a blade assortment.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor type and vibration
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored brushless motors, counterweights and soft starts. Platform reach was considered, since a battery that also runs a trimmer or drill has real value.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit across the lineup
howWeEvaluated.description: Each saw was placed by owner type, from platform owners to first-time buyers. Picks are ranked by who they suit, not by a raw score.

howToChoose.intro: Pick the saw by what you cut.
howToChoose.note: Match the blade to the material before you worry about the saw.
Bare tools are only cheap if you own the battery.

cards.text: A narrow blade, orbital set to zero or one, a soft start and a variable-speed trigger. Slow down in tight curves.

howToChoose.intro: Know the limits of budget jigsaws.

maintenance.why: Sawdust jams clamps. Blow them out. Always remove the battery first.
A dull blade strains the motor. Replace it. Worn blade rollers cause wandering cuts.
A loose shoe cuts out of square. Tighten it. Gummy resin slows the blade, so wipe it.
Heat ages cells. Avoid cars. Lubricate the roller occasionally.
Blocked vents overheat the motor. Blow them out. A cooled motor is a longer-lived motor.

faq.q: Is a cordless jigsaw strong enough?
faq.a: For plywood, trim and softwood, yes. Thick hardwood drains the battery quickly. Slow the trigger at the start of a cut and increase speed once the blade is in the work.
It helps in wood. Use zero orbit for metal and clean veneer. Clamp the work so it cannot vibrate, because a vibrating panel splinters at the underside.
A fine-tooth blade for metal and veneer, a coarse blade for softwood. Pull the battery before changing blades to avoid an accidental start.
Tape the cut line, use a fine blade, and cut from the good side with the saw's shoe flat.
Only if you own a matching battery. Otherwise a kit is cheaper.
A 4.0 Ah pack runs a long afternoon of curves, a 2.0 Ah pack about half.
